newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to meet candidate for top U.S. military job.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to meet candidate for top U.S. military job.

text.p: President Clinton was due to meet Army Gen. Henry "Hugh" Shelton Wednesday to interview him for the post of chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, administration officials said.
Shelton, a 34-year veteran who commanded the U.S. military operation in Haiti three years ago, now heads the U.S. Special Operations Command, an elite group of 47,000 Army, Navy and Air Force troops.

The officials, who asked not to be named, said Defence Secretary William Cohen would recommend Shelton replace Army Gen. John Shalikashvili as the top U.S. military officer and would accompany him to the White House Wednesday.
But the officials stressed that Clinton had not yet made any decision on the matter.

"It's close, but it's not there yet," said one official, adding that the White House had discussed the possibility of making an announcement as early as Wednesday. Another official, however, said that this now seemed unlikely.

Cohen's first choice to replace Shalikashvili, Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston, withdrew from consideration last month after disclosure of an adulterous affair more than 10 years ago when he was separated from his wife.
Ralston is vice chairman of the joint chiefs.
After Ralston withdrew, Cohen interviewed a number of other four-star candidates from all military services and said last week that he had narrowed the field to three or four.

While acknowledging that Clinton would want to interview the top candidate, McCurry declined to confirm that Shelton was scheduled to come to the White House and said the president had a right to make the decision in private.
"The president will want to think hard, and I don't know how long and hard, about a decision that is very important to every American," McCurry said at his daily briefing.

Earlier, McCurry told reporters that Clinton knew Shelton well because of his role in the Haiti operation. If approved by the Senate, Shelton would jump from leading 2 per cent of U.S. forces to running the whole show from the Pentagon.

A native of Tarboro, North Carolina, Shelton did not attend the elite U.S. Military Academy at West Point. Instead, he holds a degree in textile engineering from North Carolina State University and a master's degree from Auburn University in Alabama.
